$comment: SDLC ID Allocator — assigns each TASK a non-overlapping ID range per prefix so multiple developers / parallel TASKs cannot collide on the same ENTITY-006 / COMP-005 / etc. Replaces the scan-based PM-centralized allocation (Rule 8.7) for multi-user contexts. Single-user keeps both: allocator is primary, scan is fallback.
_rangeSize_doc: Each TASK gets {rangeSize} consecutive IDs per prefix. Default 100 means TASK-001 owns 1-100, TASK-002 owns 101-200, TASK-003 owns 201-300, etc. (visually aligned with the offset, easy to recognize at a glance). Adjust upward if a single TASK is expected to allocate more than 100 entities of a given prefix; adjust downward only if total TASK count would exhaust the 999-ID cap (a project-lifetime concern, not a daily one).
_nextOffset_doc: Counter for the next TASK's range. New TASK-NNN gets range [(nextOffset-1)*rangeSize + 1, nextOffset*rangeSize]. With rangeSize=100: offset 1 → [1,100], offset 2 → [101,200], offset 3 → [201,300]. Incremented atomically by sdlc-allocate-ids.sh. NEVER decrement — abandoned TASKs keep their range allocated forever (per Rule 8.4 永不重用 / no ID reuse, extended to ranges).
_prefixes_doc: Globally-numbered ID prefixes covered by allocator (per-TASK namespace partitioning). NOT included by design: (1) TASK-internal prefixes (FR/NFR/BR/AC/LOGIC/TEST/CR/SEC/SUG) — they reset per TASK and don't need cross-TASK range reservation. (2) ERR — error codes use the format ERR-{DOMAIN}-{NNN} where DOMAIN is a global category label (AUTH/USER/PAYMENT/...) and NNN is a per-DOMAIN sequence shared across all TASKs. ERR has no per-TASK namespace because multiple TASKs can extend the same DOMAIN; multi-user safety on ERR comes from per-DOMAIN scan in shared/error-codes.md + git push --atomic, not allocator range reservation.
_allocations_doc: Map of TASK-ID → {prefix: [start, end]} pairs. Populated by sdlc-allocate-ids.sh on /sdlc:start. Example: "TASK-001": {"ENTITY": [1, 99], "MOD": [1, 99], ...}. agents read their assigned range from PM dispatch prompt (PM grabs it from this file) and number sequentially within the range.
_history_doc: Append-only log of allocation events. Each entry: {taskId, allocatedAt, offset, ranges, abandoned (optional, true after /sdlc:abandon)}. Provides audit trail for who got which range and when. Helpful when a future TASK looks up 'why does ENTITY-237 belong to TASK-003' or when the team retrospects on range exhaustion.
